passages.original: — Postera die, inter initia diei, eorum repræsentato conventu, residentibus Constantio et Ammonio, — Arnobius dixit : Si Serapioni aliqua super- sunt de hesterno conflictu, si voluntas est : pandat. — Serapion dixit. Una quæstio evangelica noscitur remansisse, illa scilicet, quam Arius videtur a habere palmarem, cum dicit : Me quid culpant dicentem, Pater major me est (Joan. xiv, 28), cum ipse Filius de seipso testetur dicens : Pater qui misit me, major me est? — Arnobius dixit: In ea forma, in qua Filius Patris est sine matre, ipse et Pater unum sunt: in ea vero forma, in qua Filius matris est sine Patre, Patre minor est.
passages.english: — On the following day, at the beginning of the day, when their assembly had been reconvened, with Constantius and Ammonius seated, — Arnobius said: If Serapion has anything left over from yesterday's debate, let him set it out, if he wishes. — Serapion said: One question from the Gospel is known to have remained, namely the one on which Arius seems to hold the palm, when he says: Why do they blame me for saying, "The Father is greater than I" (John 14:28), when the Son himself testifies about himself, saying: "The Father who sent me is greater than I"? — Arnobius said: In that form in which he is the Son of the Father without a mother, he and the Father are one; but in that form in which he is the Son of a mother without a father, he is less than the Father.
passages.notes: The stray 'a' after 'videtur' is a footnote mark and has been omitted.

passages.original: Et adjecit : Ergo sensus fratris nostri Cyrilli in hoc quod dicit Θεοτόϰον Mariam, valde concordat, talis decet partus Deum. Deum partu Suo Virgo effudit, ipso potente qui omnipotentia plenus est. d Hilarius quoque vir acris ingenii scribens in Constantium imperatorem, de incarnatione Domini sic ait: Filius Dei factus homo Deus. Et præposterans repetit: Deus filius hominis factus est Deus, non Deus factus est homo, et filius Dominis factus est Filius Dei. Superavit enim magni- tudo Domini parvitatem servilis formae, ita ut ipsa forma servilis, quam assumpsit, cessaret esse servilis per eum Dominum qui eam assumpsit.
passages.english: And he added: "Therefore the meaning of our brother Cyril, in saying that Mary is Theotokos, agrees closely [with this]: 'Such a birth befits God.' The Virgin brought forth God by her childbearing, through the power of him who is full of omnipotence." Hilary too, a man of keen intellect, writing against the emperor Constantius, speaks thus of the Lord's incarnation: "The Son of God made man [is] God." And reversing the order he repeats: "God the son of man was made God; God was not made man, and the son of man was made Son of God. For the greatness of the Lord overcame the lowliness of the form of a servant, so that the very form of a servant which he assumed ceased to be servile, through that Lord who assumed it."
passages.notes: Stray letter 'd' before 'Hilarius' omitted as a footnote mark. 'filius Dominis' read as 'filius hominis'. The quoted passage of Hilary is confused as transmitted ("God the son of man was made God, God was not made man"); translated as it stands. 'Theotokos' = 'God-bearer'.

passages.original: Percunctanti vero mihi et discere admodum cupienti, si modeste Patrum vestigia vos quoque sectantes, fidem quoque rectam et immaculatam enilescere contendatis, conversatione autem egregia decorati religiosæ vitæ sanctis laboribus a voluntatem veram existimantes pro novo labore noviter tolerare. Et post pauca ait : b Sempiternæ memoriæ Pater noster Athanasius, qui Alexandrinæ Ecclesiæ episcopatum annis quadraginta et sex coornavit, qui profanis hæreticorum argutiis inexpugnabilem et apostolicam obtinebat sapientiam, et quasi odoratissimo unguento suis scriptis lætificat orbem terrarum, cujus fidem rectam et veram dogmatum scientiam conctorum testimonia comprobant, cum de sacrosancta Trinitate, et unius substantiæ, quod Græce dicitur ὀμοούσιον, opus componeret, in libro tertio identidem sanctam Virginem Θεοτόϰον appellat.
passages.english: "Now, as I inquired and was very eager to learn whether you too, modestly following the footsteps of the Fathers, strive to make the right and spotless faith shine forth, and, adorned with excellent conduct in the holy labours of the religious life, consider it a true wish to endure anew for a new labour..." And after a little he says: "Our Father Athanasius, of everlasting memory, who adorned the episcopate of the Church of Alexandria for forty-six years, who held an apostolic wisdom impregnable to the profane subtleties of the heretics, and who gladdens the whole world with his writings as with a most fragrant ointment, whose right faith and true knowledge of doctrines the testimonies of all confirm—when he was composing a work on the most holy Trinity and on the one substance, which in Greek is called homoousion, in the third book repeatedly calls the holy Virgin Theotokos."
passages.notes: The first sentence is syntactically incomplete and apparently corrupt; 'enilescere' read as 'enitescere' (to shine forth), and 'a voluntatem' is unclear (stray 'a' perhaps a footnote mark); rendering tentative. Stray 'b' omitted as a footnote mark.

passages.original: Nam Θεοτόϰον vult eam vocari, non Χριστοτόϰν ; aut si ano consentit, et Χριστοτόϰον pande. — Arnobius dixit : Sanctus Cyrillus contra eos qui sanctam Mariam Θεοτόϰον neganl, secutus priores suos e; iscopos Theophilum, sive Athanasium, ostendit illam Θεοτόϰν exstitisse, ne forte parem habere putaretur, cum Χριστοτόνος dicitur. b Fuerunt enim et aliæ Christolocæ, nulla tamen ita Χριστοτόϰος et Θεοτόϰος, et virgo effecta feta est sicut Maria.
passages.english: "For he wants her to be called Theotokos, not Christotokos; or if he agrees with this, explain also Christotokos." Arnobius said: "Saint Cyril, against those who deny that holy Mary is Theotokos, following his predecessors the bishops Theophilus and Athanasius, showed that she was Theotokos, lest she perhaps be thought to have an equal when she is called Christotokos. For there were also other bearers of christs, yet none so truly Christotokos and Theotokos, and none who, being a virgin, became pregnant as Mary did."
passages.notes: 'aut si ano consentit' is corrupt; read roughly as 'aut si huic/uno consentit', tentative. 'Christotokos' = 'Christ-bearer'; 'other Christotocae' presumably refers to mothers of 'anointed ones' (christs), sense uncertain. 'e; iscopos' read as 'episcopos'; 'sive' taken as 'and'. Stray 'b' omitted.

passages.original: n, 7), et idcirco miramque hominis substantiam unius Dei esse auctoris; atque ideo omnia quæ facta sunt nobis subdita sunt, quia illa jussu Dei sunt formata. Igitur non opere. De homiue autem dixisse Deum legimus : Faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram (Gen. i, 26); et ideo hominem nobilissimam Dei fabricam non solum ex anima et corpore, sed et spiritu constare, et esse triplicem Apostolus probat dicens : c Ut integer spiritus vester, et caro, et anima in adventu Dei servetur (I Thess. v, 25). Suc spiritum dico, qui accidens est, non naturalem, nec eumdem, esse in omnibus. Sic enim Apostolus dicit: Nos autem non spiritum hujus mundi accepimus, sed spiritum qui ex Deo est (I Cor. u, 12). Istum autem quem credentes accipimus, gratiae divinæ est; alterum vero spiritum intentionis diabolicæ. Quia dia- bolus non sine initio est crealus, ut Marcion delirat, sed a Deo bono angelus factus est, et omne malum ex ipso initium sumpsit.
passages.english: [...] 2:7), and therefore that the wonderful substance of man has one God as its author; and so all things that have been made are subject to us, because they were formed by God's command. Therefore not by labour. But of man we read that God said: "Let us make man in our image and likeness" (Gen. 1:26); and therefore the Apostle proves that man, God's noblest workmanship, consists not only of soul and body but also of spirit, and is threefold, saying: "That your spirit, and flesh, and soul may be kept whole at the coming of God" (1 Thess. 5:23). I say that this spirit is accidental, not natural, and not the same in all. For so the Apostle says: "But we have not received the spirit of this world, but the spirit which is from God" (1 Cor. 2:12). This [spirit] which we receive as believers is of divine grace; but the other spirit is of diabolical intent. For the devil was not created without beginning, as Marcion raves, but was made an angel by the good God, and all evil took its beginning from him.
passages.notes: The passage opens mid-reference (the citation is Gen. 2:7, continuing from the context). 'miramque' is taken as 'miram'. 'Igitur non opere' ('therefore not by labour') is elliptical and possibly corrupt; the sense seems to be that things were made by command rather than by handiwork. 'Suc' is read as 'Hunc' ('this'). The edition's reference I Thess. v, 25 should be 5:23. The stray 'c' before 'Ut' is a footnote mark and has been omitted.

passages.original: XXX.—Serapion dixit: Non ita docentem Augustinum audivi. — Arnobius dixit: In qua parte non ita audisti eum docentem ? — Serapion dixit : Non imperium legis implere omnia volumina tractatuum et librornm ejus testantur scripta. — Arnobius dixit : Tangit me ita sicut sunt mira ejus verba in medium proferre, et probare quantum legis imperio, quantum libero concedatur arbitrio.
passages.english: XXX.—Serapion said: "I have not heard Augustine teaching thus." Arnobius said: "In what part have you not heard him teaching thus?" Serapion said: "The writings of all the volumes of his treatises and books testify that the command of the law does not fulfil everything." Arnobius said: "I am moved to bring forward his wonderful words just as they are, and to prove how much is granted to the command of the law and how much to free will."
passages.notes: Serapion's second statement is awkwardly phrased and may be corrupt; rendering tentative.
